title: Why a wooden spoon stops a pot boiling over
pause_note: Channel v5, Kitchen Science. WEIRD + DO hook: foam already at the rim at 0 s, a spoon drops on and the foam backs off by ~1.5 s; wrong guess (it presses the foam down) killed at ~4 s; reveal at ~7 s (macro: bubbles touching the dry wood burst); cause (starch skin), chain reaction, consequence (hot wet spoon stops working, foam spills), loop to the foaming pot; one-word question.

beats: This pot of pasta is about to boil over. Put a wooden spoon across it, and the foam backs off.
It is not pushing the foam down. Watch where the bubbles touch it.
Every bubble that hits the dry, cooler wood bursts.
Starch from the pasta makes each bubble sticky, so they stack up instead of popping.
The spoon breaks the top ones, and each burst knocks out its neighbours.
But once the spoon is hot and soaked, it stops working, and the foam climbs over.
